The note is incorrect: in Habermas, "law as medium" means formally rational steering rules that coordinate the economic and administrative systems through money and power, while "law as institution" means lifeworld-rooted norms (e.g., constitutional rights, family law) that depend on communicative justification and sustain solidarity. The distinction contrasts system-integrating instrumental law with normative law protecting the lifeworld, not media channels versus courts.
CONFIDENCE: 95
